name: NuMoon
summary: A lunar-radio programme used the Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope to set limits on neutrinos above 10^22 eV, and developed a lower-frequency search strategy for LOFAR.
detection_principle: Askaryan radio pulses from showers in the lunar regolith are sought in two telescope beams on the Moon. At wavelengths comparable to shower dimensions the emission is less narrowly beamed, increasing the effective aperture at extreme energies.

sites.name: Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope, Drenthe, Netherlands
sites.location: Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope, Drenthe, Netherlands

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: The WSRT measurement is a completed historical campaign. LOFAR follow-up is described as technology development in the cited 2015 contribution; present-day dedicated lunar observing status is not established.

timeline.event: WSRT lunar observing campaigns provided the published exposure.
Neutrino limits from WSRT lunar observations published.
LOFAR implementation and trigger developments reported.

collaboration.name: NuMoon Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

key_parameters.name: WSRT observing mode
key_parameters.value: Two beams on different parts of the Moon, each with four frequency sub-bands

results.summary: After interference rejection the WSRT sample yielded a 90% confidence upper limit on the ultra-high-energy neutrino flux, without a neutrino discovery.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.

media.caption: Published NuMoon WSRT neutrino-flux upper limits from the 46.7-hour sample (2010 paper, Figure 12); this is a result plot, not a detected neutrino spectrum.
